title: The Internet Doesn't Come From Satellites! 🌊
description: Most of the world's internet travels through cables on the ocean floor, about as thick as a garden hose! Meet the hidden network that runs our lives.

scenes.say: Think your internet comes from satellites? Actually, most of it comes from the bottom of the sea!
scenes.image: File:Landing of the submarine cable, Port Darwin, 7 November 1871(GN01968).jpg

scenes.label: Travels through undersea cables
scenes.say: More than ninety-five percent of internet data between continents travels through cables lying on the ocean floor.

scenes.caption: Data as light
scenes.say: Inside each cable are glass fibers thinner than a hair, and your data races through them as pulses of light.

right.label: In the deep
right.sub: About as thick as a garden hose

scenes.say: In the deep ocean, a cable is about as thick as a garden hose. Near the shore it's thicker and armored to protect it from ship anchors.
Fun fact: sharks have bitten some of these cables, so companies wrap them in extra protective layers.
